1. PURPOSE
1.1. To set procedural guidelines on how to admit patient in intensive care unit.
1.2. To determine patient who need ICU care according to priorities in accordance to ICU bed capacity
1.3. To avoid unnecessary admission of patient in lCU.
1.4. To provide advance monitoring and intensive treatment for all medical and surgical patients
2. DEFINITION & ABBREVIATION
2.1. lntensive care - refers to the specialized treatment given to patients who are acutely unwell and
require critical medical care.
2.2. lntensive Care Unit (lCU) - provides the critical care and life support for acutely ill and injured
patients
2.3. Designee - is a person selected or designated to carry out a duty or role.
2.4. NOD - Nurse on Duty
2.5. APACHE (Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation) ll SCORE - Provides a robust method
for classifling the severity of illness in critically ill patients.

4.1. Admission to ICU will be according to criteria and priorities.
4.2. APACHE II
4.2.1. Purpose: Define patient inclusion criteria and timing (usually within the first 24hours of ICU
admission).
4.2.2. Data Collection :
4.2.2.1. Mandate recording of 12 routine physiological measurements : (Temperature,
Mean Arterial Pressure, Heart Rate, Respiratory Rate, Oxygenation, Arterial PH,
Serum Sodium, Serum Potassium, Serum Creatinine, Hematocrit, WBC Count and
Clasgow Coma Scale),
4.2.2.2. Age point: Points are added based on the patient's age.
4.2.2.3. Chronic health points: Points are added if the patient has a history of severe organ
system insufficiency or is immunocompromised.
4.2.3. Risk Stratification : Predicts the statistical risk of patient mortality in lntensive care unit
4.3- Categories of patient qualified for admission or transfer to ICU
4.3.1. Multiple trauma including e.g. head injuries
4.3.2. Penetrating wounds in the chest and abdomen that are hemodynamically unstable.
4.3.3. Respiratory failure (who are in need for immediate ventilator support)
4.3.4. Shock not responding to initial fluid resuscitation.
4.3.5. Critically ill patients transferred from another hospital
4.3.6. Drug overdose (who are clinically unstable)

4.3.7.2. Patient with ejection fraction of less tha n 30%

and Removal
1.2. To provide procedural guidance to all staff on care and use of CVAD including dealing with any
problems encountered.
1.3. To prevent infection in collaboration with infection Control in patients with CVAD.
1.4. To establish protocol on how to maintain patency of Central Venous Access Device.
2. DEFINITION & ABBREVIATION
2.1. Central Venous Access Device (CVAD) - also known as Central Line, Central Venous Line or Central
Venous Catheter. lt is a multipurpose venous catheter that terminates at or close to the heart or in
one of the great vessels. lt is placed into a large vein in the neck (lnternal Jugular Vein), chest
(Subclavian Vein or Axillary Vein), and groin (Femoral Vein).
2.2. Aseptic Technique -a procedure used by medical staff to prevent the spread of infection
2.3. PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) - an equipment that will protect the staff against health or
safety risks at work
2.4. Hand Hygiene (HH) - a general term that applies to routine hand washing, antiseptic hand wash,
antiseptic hand rub, or surgical hand antisepsis.
2.5. Valsalva maneuver - forced expiratory effort against a closed glottis that decreases intrathoracic
pressure, hampering venous return to the heart, and that can be used to inflate the Eustachian
tubes and adjust pressure in the middle ear.
2.6. MCC - Medica Cloud care system (Hts - Hospital tnformation system)

2.1. Neurological Assessment- monitors a critically ill patient's nervous system function and includes
evaluatingthe levelof consciousness, motor responses, pupillaryfunction, and vitalsigns.
2.2. Level of Consciousness (LOC) - Assess mental status using tools like the AVPU scale (Alert, Verbal,

2.3. Motor Function - Evaluate the patient's ability to move extremities, check for strength, and assess
reflexes.

2.5. Cranial Nerves - Assess cranial nerve function, which is important for understanding neurological
status.

their responsiveness to stimuli: Alert, responds to Voice, responds to Pain, or Unresponsive.
2.7. Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)- is a neurological scale that aims to give a reliable or objective way of
recording the conscious state of a person for initial as well as subsequent assessment.
2.8. Lunula - is the crescent-shaped whitish area of the bed of a fingernail or toenail.

a. To determine baseline data of the infant's condition, to provide prompt therapy 
and life saving measures and perform assessment, planning and intervention that

2. Scope  
a. Case accepted and admission ordered by the Consultant. 
b. Proper documentation of the procedure and report for any abnormality 
3. Definition 
a. Admission of an infant to NICU: A neonate should be admitted to NICU when the 
baby is unstable and need high dependency care continuously from the medical 
and nursing staff 
4. Abbreviation: 
a. NICU - Neonatal Intensive Care Unit 
5. Policy Statement 
a. All admissions must have a written physician's order. 
b. Emergency equipment, as in ventilator must always be ready for admission. 
c. Admission to NICU is categorized as; 
i. Infants requiring cardiopulmonary resuscitation. 
ii. Infants requiring prolong mechanical ventilation 
iii. Infants who are critically ill, preferably clean cases. 
iv. Seriously ill infants delivered from delivery room without suspected 
maternal infection. 
v. Infants requiring close observation and monitoring, infants with metabolic 
disorders. 
vi. Infants below 37 weeks of gestational age. 
vii. Infants with life threatening surgery. 
viii. High risk infants requiring extensive sophisticated equipment.

Rationale

dosage, route and time intervals) 
For safe drug administration and 
patient's safety.  
2. Admit infant without delay in order to 
administer immediate treatment. 
Delays in the treatment possess 
multitude consequences especially for 
neonates. 
3. Place the infant under preheated 
radiant warmer. 
To stabilize the patient's temperature 
and avoid hypothermia. 
4. Wash hands and dry infants. 
To reduce the transmission of 
microorganism and dry hands to 
prevent further hypothermia

1. Purpose 
a. Obtain CSF for examination purposes such as protein, glucose, analysis and 
culture 
b. Measuring cerebrospinal pressure and assisting detection of observation of CSF 
circulation. 
2. Scope  
a. First Step: 
i. Physician explains the procedure and obtains consent. 
b. Last Step: 
i. Appropriate sample sent to the laboratory. 
3. Definition 
a. Lumbar Puncture is a diagnostic and at times therapeutic procedure that is 
performed in order to collect a sample of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for 
biochemical, microbiological, and cytological analysis, or to relieve increased 
intracranial pressure. 
b. Cerebrospinal Fluid is a clear, colorless, bodily fluid that occupies the 
subarachnoid space and the ventricular system around and inside the brain and 
spinal cord.

b. CSF – Cerebrospinal Fluid

a. Procedure must be performed by a physician with written order and must be 
assisted by a registered staff nurse. 
b. NICU admission consent must be signed by the parents upon admission. 
c. Procedure requires sterile technique and careful patient positionin8. 
d. Lumbar puncture should not be done to patient with lumbar deformity and 
infection at the site of puncture. 
e. It should be performed cautiously in patient with increased intracranial pressure. 
f. Prepare sedation drugs as preferred by the physician.

1. Purpose 
a. To establish a guideline in giving bath to an infant inside an incubator that will 
provide and maintain normal body temperature while promoting the well-being of 
the infant 
2. Scope  
a. First Step 
i. Assess the need of giving bath to the infant 
b. Last Step 
i. Documentation of response to the procedure. 
3. Definition 
a. Baiting of an infant - Bathing of an infant is defined as cleaning of the body for 
the purposes of relaxation cleanliness and healing. 
b. Umbilical cord - is the connecting cord from the developing embryo or fetus to 
the placenta that supplies oxygen, nutrients and a means of waste elimination 
while the fetus is inside the womb. 
4. Abbreviation: 
a. RN - Registered Nurse 
b. IV - lnt6ravenous 
c. MRN - Medical Record Number 
d. OGT - Orogastric tube 
5. Policy Statements 
a. Infants with the following clinical conditions must be given bath inside the 
incubator: 
i. With cardiac monitor 
ii. With oxygen and IV therapy 
iii. Preterm infant with a weight of less than 1.800 kilograms 
iv. Post operatively patients 
v. IV sites, wound sites or any break in the skin must not be immersed or 
soaked in water 
b. Standard precautions are to be followed during the procedure. 
c. Proper identification should commence prior to bath.

1. Purpose 
a. To have a clear guidance in ensuring the prevention and management of 
intravenous infiltration, Phlebitis and Extravasation is standardized in the 
pediatric intensive care unit. 
b. All staff act in accordance with this policy to prevent the development of 
intravenous Infiltration, Phlebitis and Extravasation. 
2. Scope  
a. First Step 
i. Assess patient for any presence or risk for developing infiltration, 
Phlebitis and Extravasation. 
b. Last Step 
i. Document the assessment, preventive measures and management of 
infiltration, Phlebitis and Extravasation. 
3. Definition 
a. Phlebitis is defined as an inflammation of the vein, is among the most common 
complications of IV therapy. Possible causes of phlebitis may be chemical 
(caused by the substance being infused), mechanical (movement of the catheter 
while inside the vein) or bacterial (either intrinsic or extrinsic). 
b. Infiltration is the leaking of IV fluid into the tissue surrounding the vein. This 
occurs when IV fluids continue to be delivered even though the tip of the catheter 
is no longer in the vessel or is blocked. Although most infiltrations do not cause 
tissue damage, the potential for serious harm does exist. When a large amount of 
IV solution enters the tissues, nerve compression injuries from compartment 
syndrome can result. 
c. Extravasation is an infiltration involving the leakage of vesicant fluids into the 
tissues. Vesicants are substances known to be more caustic than regular lV fluids, 
and are capable of causing physical harm unless they are kept strictly in the 
vascular space. These chemical or drug substances can cause blistering and 
burning in the tissue Vesicants include Calcium Chloride, Potassium Chloride, 
Sodium Chloride, Calcium Gluconate, Dobutamine, Diazepam, Dopamine, 
Norepinephrine (Levophed), Phenytoin (Dilantin), Promethazine (Phenergan), 
Propofol, Vasopressin, Radiologic contrast agents etc. 
4. Abbreviation: 
a. IV - Intravenous 
5. Policy Statements 
a. The infusion site must be inspected every 30-60 minutes and documented when in 
use and if extravasation or infiltration is suspected. Observe for any erythema or 
edema. 
b. The port needle entry site should be observed before administering vesicants ot 
irritant solutions.
